title: Pyspark Dataframe repartition strategy
question:
Lets say I have a very large dataframe df. Now I have two smaller dataframes df1 and df2. df is getting joined with df1 based on key1. And df2 is getting joined with key2 and key3.

Now I know salting is technique could be used in such case. But lets say I want to repartition df and broadcast df2 and df1.

So in such case should I call once

df.repartition("key1","key2","key3") and then join df1 and df2 with df?

or first I repartition by key1 and join with df

df.repartition("key1).join df1

then again

df.repartition("key2","key3").join df2
answer:
I think if you repartition only once with the 3 keys, it will be more efficient as it:

  • Shuffls only once vs two times shuffling
  • Avoids data skew, since key1 could produce much more bigger size partitions, but adding key2 and key3 should split more bigger partitions
df.repartition("key1","key2","key3") and then join df1 and df2 with df?

If this is an inner join, then choose the first join as the one that can eliminate the most data and follow with the other df
